sources.entry: Intel Intrinsics Guide - Maps each intrinsic to its instruction and CPUID flag, with the vendor's latency and throughput per microarchitecture.

summary.title: Intel® Intrinsics Guide
summary.one_liner: Look up any Intel SIMD intrinsic to see its C header, underlying assembly instruction, required CPUID flags, and vendor latency/throughput per microarchitecture.
keywords: which cpu feature flag does an intrinsic need
takeaways: Each intrinsic entry gives a C synopsis (header such as immintrin.h), the assembly instruction it maps to, and the required CPUID flags.
Latency and throughput (CPI) tables list values per Intel microarchitecture such as Skylake, Icelake, Sapphire Rapids and Alderlake.
Masked ({k}) and zeroing ({z}) variants of AVX-512 instructions are listed separately, and their latency can differ from the unmasked form.
Data is sourced from Intel's 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals, per the page.
summary.summary: The Intel Intrinsics Guide is an interactive reference for C-style functions that expose x86 instructions without writing assembly. This captured page shows entries grouped by instruction family, including AVX-512 VP2INTERSECT, RAO-INT, SSSE3 pabs, AVX-512 vpabs and vpand variants. Each entry lists the header to include, the instruction form, the CPUID feature flags, a description and operation, and, where available, a latency and throughput table by microarchitecture. The page text is mostly the reference listing itself, with the version dated 07/12/2024 (3.6.9); the description and operation sections are empty in this capture.
